correctness.rationale: Characterized nearest points by equality in triangle inequality: interior inputs fixed and exterior positive-sign coordinate shrinkages with output norm r. Soft threshold exists uniquely for any ell1 input, with finite active set above positive tau even for arbitrary infinite I. Finite-dimensional sign-cell Jacobian is a sign conjugate of C_k=I−11^T/k on active coordinates, with induced ell1 norm 2−2/k, giving optimal upper bound (and exact slope realization). For any selector its value near b=(1/n,...,1/n) must be compared to n fixed boundary inputs at ell1 distance epsilon; the unrestricted zero-sum minimax is convex and symmetric, reduces to q=(a,−a/(n−1),...), and minimizes max(2a,2−2a/(n−1)) at a=(n−1)/n, so all selectors have modulus >=2−2/n. Finite supports force infinite lower bound 2; countable-support truncation yields upper bound 2. Exact rational minimax witnesses recomputed, not substitutes for universal proof.

value.rationale: Sharp optimal Lipschitz constants of arbitrary nearest-point selections are a natural multivalued variational analysis invariant, not merely a chosen algorithm’s modulus. The theorem proves a universal nonlinear/asymmetric lower bound and exact finite/infinite dimension threshold for nonexpansiveness; both geometric obstruction and limit are useful structural facts.

final_claim: Over all single-valued nearest-point selections from real ell1(I) onto its radius-r closed ell1 ball, the exact infimum of global Lipschitz constants is 1 for |I|=1, 2−2/n for finite n>=2, and 2 for every infinite I, attained by coordinatewise soft thresholding.
limitations: Real scalar ell1 spaces and metric selection onto centered norm balls; not complex field/general convex targets.
